seo_title: Cost of Living in Bangkok 2026: Visa, Prices, Reviews | Relocost
seo_description: How much does it cost to live in Bangkok per month, do Russians need a visa, work, rent and reviews from those who relocated. A realistic moving budget in the Relocost calculator.
intro_text: Cheap and delicious street food, convenient transport, and quality healthcare at reasonable prices. One of the best Asian cities for a long winter stay or a freelancer's relocation.
pros: Cheap and tasty street food — lunch for 250 ₽
Plenty of long-term visas — LTR, DTV, ED
cons: Smog season from January to April
Traffic jams beyond the BTS radius
The language barrier is stronger than it seems

best_places.name: Sukhumvit (Asok–Phrom Phong)
best_places.description: The best apartments near the BTS for expats — restaurants, gyms and an English-speaking environment.

best_places.name: Ari
best_places.description: A trendy district with young Thais, third-wave coffee shops and creative little stores.

best_places.name: Chatuchak Market
best_places.description: The largest weekend market in Southeast Asia — clothes, food and antiques.

best_places.name: Hubba-To
best_places.description: A large coworking space with a conference room, suited to teams and meetups.

visa_steps.title: Visa-free entry
visa_steps.description: 30 days on arrival for Russian citizens, extendable by 30 days at immigration.

visa_steps.title: Tourist Visa TR
visa_steps.description: 60 days through the consulate, with a 30-day extension available in Thailand.

visa_steps.title: Long-Term Resident (LTR)
visa_steps.description: 10 years for remote workers earning from $80,000 — a premium visa with perks.

visa_steps.title: Destination Thailand Visa (DTV)
visa_steps.description: 5 years for digital nomads — launched in 2024, with minimal requirements of $14,000 in the bank.

visa_steps.title: Education Visa (ED)
visa_steps.description: 1 year for language-school students — a popular grey-zone path for long stays.

faq.question: Which bank should I choose in Bangkok?
faq.answer: Bangkok Bank — the most foreigner-friendly, opening an account with a visa and a visa sticker.

faq.question: Does the MIR card work in Bangkok?
faq.answer: No, only Visa/Mastercard or a local card.

faq.question: How much does private insurance cost in Bangkok?
faq.answer: From $800 a year for a basic plan at Bumrungrad or Bangkok Hospital.

faq.question: Where should a foreigner live in Bangkok?
faq.answer: Sukhumvit or Sathorn — close to the BTS, convenient for remote work and services.

faq.question: How is English in Bangkok?
faq.answer: It's fine in the centre, but in the outskirts you'll need basic Thai phrases or Google Translate.

faq.question: How much does a motorbike taxi cost in Bangkok?
faq.answer: 50–100 ₽ for 3 km — the fastest way to get around the traffic jams.

reviews.text: Bangkok is convenience multiplied by prices. Cheap world-class healthcare, the BTS, thousands of cafés. The downside — the English-speaking environment is limited to a few districts.
The DTV visa solved everything — 5 years of legal residence. Bangkok is noisy, but it has the energy of New York.
